analysis.title: What Matters Today: Tech Rotation, FCF Inflection, Labor/AI, Alphabet, Microsoft, AI Health Care, FOMC Recap
key_insights: Hyperscaler earnings were mixed on headline execution. One mega cap platform fell about 10% after hours on consumer ad misses even as Cloud growth stayed strong. A second beat cloud whispers, posted positive quarterly FCF and grew contracted obligations. Its light capex reflected third-party facility delivery timing, with next quarter guided higher.

Oracle rallied double digits after management outlined positive FCF in H2 FY28 and $30bn+ in FY29, with capex stepping down in FY29. Incremental capital raises are capped at $20bn through FY30, excluding refinancing. GS calls it potentially very significant for levered AI credit, but spreads have not yet responded.

Oracle guided to non-GAAP operating margins of 40%+ by FY30 on $225bn+ revenue, with high-20s project returns on a fully ramped gigawatt and about $16bn annualized revenue per fully ramped gigawatt. GS says this depends on execution, utilization and financing assumptions.

GS sees a possible pain trade of hyperscalers underperforming while de-risked picks and shovels start working. Advantest's upgrade and supportive overnight optical developments help the broader group. GS describes the market as moving from rewarding capex growth to demanding evidence of returns, and expects dips to be bought.
Credit is the most important thing to watch. Stability is improving, and Oracle is potentially more consequential for the levered infrastructure complex than either hyperscaler print.
A possible US/Iran meeting before the midterms is described as a geopolitical lottery ticket and an enormous positive surprise if it happens.

Alphabet's Search & Other revenue missed GS and Street estimates. Management cited FX headwinds and tougher comparisons as the lapping of the Search acceleration. Cloud revenue grew 103% y/y and backlog reached $561bn (+256% y/y), with about 55% expected to convert to revenue within 24 months. Compute availability is the gating factor for faster growth.

Alphabet reiterated 2026 capex guidance of $195-205bn (GS estimate about $203bn) and expects a further material increase in 2027 (not guided, GS estimate about $350bn). Management expects ROIC to stay meaningfully above cost of capital while acknowledging the disconnect in free cash flow from investing to close compute constraints.

GS reiterates Buy on Alphabet and cuts its 12-month price target from $435 to $385 on updated forward operating estimates. Management framed agentic AI (Universal Cart, Gemini Agent in Search and Workspace, expansion across Chrome and Android) as additive to Search.

Microsoft 1QFY revenue was $92.3bn (+19% cc y/y), 2% above the Street. Non-GAAP EPS was $4.89 (+27% y/y), 3% above the Street. GS says investor focus has shifted to the sustainability of token demand, token economics and the depth of financing markets.

Microsoft Copilot revenue growth accelerated q/q, daily users rose about 50% q/q, and customers consuming Copilot credits through usage-based billing rose 75. Microsoft's enterprise AI framework lets customers use the latest frontier model, route dynamically across models on quality, speed and cost, or train proprietary models on customer traces, including with MAI.
Azure grew 48% in 1Q. Despite a delay in third-party capacity shifting into 2H, Microsoft guided to 49-50% cc growth in 2Q, with demand exceeding supply and growth broad based.

AI's impact on drug development appears broad rather than concentrated in discovery, with reported gains in molecule design, lab optimization, manufacturing documentation, regulatory drafting and trial planning. Nearly all evidence is preclinical or operational, with no human clinical data yet. GS says benefits may go to healthcare companies applying AI across R&D and operations, and it is focused on the rebalanced AI Health Care Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCAIP).

The FOMC left the funds rate unchanged at its October meeting. GS expects a second and final hike in December under an every-other-meeting pace, with a third hike in March possible if inflation comes in higher than expected.

Chairman Warsh described the economy and labor market as strong but not running too hot, said inflation compensation and expectations moved in the right direction, and said financial conditions have tightened but are not tight. The FOMC keeps eight meetings a year, but one meeting in 2027 and two in 2028 will focus on strategy with no statement or rate vote. Task forces have a year-end deadline.

1QFY revenue and non-GAAP EPS beat the Street by 2% and 3%. Azure growth is guided to 49-50% cc in 2Q.
The stock rallied double digits on a path to positive FCF in H2 FY28 and a capex step-down in FY29. Capital raises are capped at $20bn through FY30.
Advantest was upgraded, which GS says reinforces the picks-and-shovels micro picture.

sector_views.rationale: Rotation from rewarding capex growth to demanding evidence of returns. GS expects hyperscalers to underperform while de-risked picks and shovels start working, and expects dips to be bought.
GS is bullish on AI in health care and focuses on the AI Health Care Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCAIP), which shows low correlation to AI, rates and oil.
